found_values.value: The one input a panel setting picks fills the BENCH rpm register and feeds the motor stall action. The panel already enables and places a rotation input by setting ('Optical tacho', 'Tacho pin'), and the BENCH page carries one rpm register with one valid bit. Hardware consequence: every rotation input keeps its own front end and GPIO, none is multiplexed, so any one can be picked. Derived from the tree; no owner figure

65,535 rpm, the highest speed the BENCH rpm register carries: to_u16 saturates there. The owner's V225 answer uses the same figure as the highest rpm ('2.54 us of delay variation at 65,535 rpm'), and the owner's V225 decision of 2026-09-29 keeps 1 degree at the highest rpm. Consequences: once-per-revolution inputs and the vibration fundamental reach 1,092 Hz; an input at the motor's electrical frequency reaches 22,937 Hz at 21 pole pairs (MOTOR_POLES even, 2 to 42). For comparison, a commercial stand's optical probe reads up to 30,000 rpm (Flight Stand 50 datasheet: 'RPM: up to 30,000 RPM') and its electrical probe 0 to 190k eRPM (Series 1585 datasheet page 3)

The specification requires an analogue sensor into an ADC on the IO board and requires the accelerometer and the index pulse to be sampled on one timebase on the coprocessor. A digital accelerometer samples on its own oscillator, so its sampling instant is not on the coprocessor's timebase

report.value: Two PIO state machines in one RP2354B PIO block, one per channel, run one copy of quad_edge.pio (19 instruction words); no external decoder, no DMA channel, no PWM slice for A and B. Each edge takes at most 6 clk_sys cycles (40 ns at 150 MHz) against 100 ns between edges at 5 MHz a channel (80 ns at 40/60 duty), so 2 state machines decode 20 Mcounts/s; 1 MHz single-ended is 4 Mcounts/s. A cycle model with the 2-flip-flop input synchroniser decodes 40,000 counts at 5 MHz without error for A-to-B spacing 30 to 70 ns, duty 40 to 60 %, 3 ns jitter and 200 reversals, and 1 MHz with 50 reversals; it holds down to 14 ns of A-to-B spacing and fails at 13 ns (AM26LV32EIDR adds 9 ns maximum part-to-part skew to the 50 ns quadrature spacing). The counts sit in the RX FIFO in put mode, read at any time; net = Y(A) - X(A) + X(B) - Y(B) modulo 2^32; a read while the shaft turns can mix counts a few edges apart, and the error does not accumulate. The index I is captured by a GPIO edge interrupt on the 1 us system timer or counted on a PWM slice's B pin. pico-examples' one-state-machine quadrature_encoder reads only sysclk / 10 = 15 Msteps/s. No quadrature decoder from an allowlisted maker is in the jlcparts copy. Derived from the datasheet's instruction timing and the model; not run on hardware; the program is not in the tree
